author: Jayden Payne
title: Lawmakers should listen to the next generation | | wvnews.com
text:
In just a few weeks, I will be packing up and leaving West Virginia to go back to college out of state. Like thousands of other students during this time of year, I am excited for what’s next, but I am also leaving the place I have called home my entire life. This problem is not unique to most people in my generation, as West Virginia has seen a population decline for decades. Policy leaders must be challenged to find solutions to reverse the so-called “struggle to stay.” If they are successful, we can reverse a trend that is troubling for the Mountain State. But first we need to examine why young people, like myself, continue to leave.
Before this summer, I probably would have blamed my departure from West Virginia on better opportunities elsewhere. But then, I spent the last few months interning with the West Virginia State Treasurer’s Office. While we still need better job opportunities, the situation in West Virginia is less dire than I originally thought. All we need to do is build foundational wealth right here in the Mountain State.
